title: WoW Exists Because Blizzard Was Addicted to EverQuest
hook: Around 1999 Blizzard scrapped a squad game called Nomad and started World of Warcraft within days, partly because so much of the studio was busy raiding in EverQuest. Which MMO pulled you in first?

script: Did you know World of Warcraft only exists because Blizzard's developers were hooked on EverQuest? In the late nineteen nineties, Blizzard's second team was building a squad based, post apocalyptic game codenamed Nomad. The team struggled to find the fun in it. Meanwhile, a lot of the studio was playing EverQuest, which had launched in nineteen ninety nine. Blizzard's own developers were in its beta, and some of them ran one of the top guilds in the game. Lead designer Rob Pardo led that guild, Legacy of Steel, while he was working on Warcraft Three. Members of the team pitched a simple idea. Why not make a game like EverQuest, but set in Warcraft, and easier to get into? Within days, Nomad was cancelled and work on World of Warcraft began. Blizzard even hired from the EverQuest community. Jeff Kaplan, an officer in Legacy of Steel, joined in May two thousand two after months of lunches that were really job interviews. He went on to lead the game, and later directed Overwatch. Blizzard revealed World of Warcraft in London in September 2001, and it launched on November 23, 2004. That was roughly five years of work by a team of about fifty to sixty people. Follow for more gaming history.
